key_insight: Adaptive Algorithmic Control (A2C) reallocates finite quantum computational effort based on a state-derived proxy so that cumulative hardness is equalized, not physical time.
engineering_relevance: This suggests quantum performance can be improved by software-level control policies that optimize resource allocation under fixed depth and measurement budgets, complementing hardware advances.
method: Uses a State-Proxy Equalization theorem to determine the optimal allocation rule for proxy-error minimization.
Infers computational hardness directly from the evolving quantum state without reconstructing the full many-body spectrum.
Applies adaptive control during quantum simulations and hardware runs to redistribute effort across the computation.
evidence_signal: Across problems up to 156 qubits, the method improved low-energy sampling probabilities by 22% to over 100,000% under matched circuit depths and measurement budgets, using exact simulations, supercomputer runs, and IBM hardware experiments.
watch_item: The approach depends on accurate state-derived hardness proxies, so practical performance may be limited by proxy estimation error and control overhead on real devices.
paper_title: Beyond Hardware: Adaptive Algorithmic Control by State-Proxy Equalization
